beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. The entry point takes --url out first, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Two commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder, whose headless browser opens the server's own page: the page plays the walkthrough, the Codex voice narrates it, and the tab's capture becomes the video file.

nodes.name: Command contract

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.name: Record
nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts).

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. The entry point takes --url out first, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.name: Source checkout
nodes.responsibility: Which archboard checkout this process runs and the port of its server: 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree; hands a command to the bin/archboard of the checkout it stands in
nodes.description: The main checkout has a .git directory; a linked worktree has a .git file and takes 10000 + sha256(root path) mod 10000. The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. The hand-off follows the working directory, not -C, and does not happen when the environment sets ARCHBOARD_URL: the URL already names the server, and every Codex thread sets it, so a workhorse in another archboard checkout runs the server's own source (ADR 0050). beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. nodes.name: Replay

nodes.name: Install skill

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.name: Inspect

nodes.name: Rename

nodes.name: Record
nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. nodes.name: Status
nodes.responsibility: status: whether the Archboard server answers, who it is, and what it reports

nodes.name: Replay

nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. nodes.name: Command contract
nodes.responsibility: Runs one bound command contract: parse, prerequisites, handler, presentation; callers reach it only through its root files
nodes.description: Callers outside import only the root files of src/cli/command-contract. runner.ts exports runCommand, the one call the router makes; it passes straight on to executeCommand in lib/execution.ts, which is private. bootstrap.ts and status.ts are root files too: the bootstrap bin.ts runs first, and the status command contract.

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.name: Locality
nodes.responsibility: Ranks parts by commits that changed their bound declarations or paths, labels path-wide fallback, and lists pairs that change together

nodes.name: Footprint
nodes.responsibility: Prints the parts a commit range changed against a proposal, with declaration attribution or explicit path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Server launcher
nodes.responsibility: Starts the Archboard server, which needs no vault, as a detached child when nothing answers, and stops it

nodes.name: Prerequisites
nodes.responsibility: Makes sure what a command needs is there: the server, started when it is not running, and an open canvas

nodes.name: Image clipboard
nodes.responsibility: Publishes PNG and HTML to the native desktop clipboard; retains Linux ownership until another copy replaces it
nodes.description: Uses @teddyzhu/clipboard on Linux and macOS. A detached Bun process owns Linux clipboard data after the command exits. macOS retains the data itself.

nodes.name: Clipboard image
nodes.responsibility: Builds escaped image HTML and its accessible description from the captured board

nodes.name: Source checkout
nodes.responsibility: Which archboard checkout this process runs and the port of its server: 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree; hands a command to the bin/archboard of the checkout it stands in
nodes.description: The main checkout has a .git directory; a linked worktree has a .git file and takes 10000 + sha256(root path) mod 10000. The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. nodes.name: Move
nodes.responsibility: semantic move: the whole board into the vault found from --to, as -C finds one, and every drill-down the move rewrote
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051. --expect-version is required, as for every write. A --to holder the registry does not know is registered, and the answer says so. A move that stopped part way names the drill-downs it rewrote already; the same move run again finishes it.

nodes.name: Removed variables
nodes.responsibility: Names the environment variables archboard no longer reads and the refusal for each, which says what to do instead

nodes.name: Repository setup
nodes.responsibility: Makes the .archboard/vault of the git checkout that holds the directory when it has none, and takes the block an earlier version wrote out of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, changing nothing else in the file
nodes.description: Only a begin marker and an end marker that each stand on a line of their own bound a block, across CRLF line endings and never past another begin marker. A marker quoted inside a line is prose and stays, and so does a begin marker whose end marker is gone.

nodes.name: Command startup
nodes.responsibility: Takes argv from the process to one selected command: hands over to the checkout whose source runs, refuses a removed environment variable, finds the command in the table and bounds its run

nodes.name: Server access
nodes.responsibility: Every reach to the Archboard server: the one request path, the board routes with their refusals, starting the server when nothing answers, and restarting it on a new bundle

nodes.name: Pictures and video
nodes.responsibility: What a command produces as a picture or a video outside the server: a headless browser makes the PNG, the recorder makes the narrated video, and the clipboard takes the image

nodes.name: Views
nodes.responsibility: views: every view of a board, with what each draws at a variant
nodes.description: Draws the overview, every authored view and Everything through the render route that render uses, and reports for each what the picture places (nodes, edges, flows and steps), the marks its key counts and its size. A view that draws nothing on the variant is listed with nothing drawn. --variant, --against and --no-comparison read as render reads them.

nodes.name: Restart
nodes.responsibility: Stops the server, builds the frontend of the checkout this process runs with bun run build:frontend, and starts the server again
nodes.description: It refuses a server that it could not start again before it stops it, and a refused stop leaves the bundle unbuilt. A failed build refuses with FRONTEND_BUILD_FAILED, carries the build's output and says that the server is stopped. The answer names the entry script of the new bundle, as /health reports it.

nodes.name: Invocation context
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the board, vault, doing line, expected version, and writing session for one CLI invocation

nodes.name: Historical correction
nodes.responsibility: Suggests historical commits, previews corrections and writes checked corrections

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, claims and panes through theirs, and the server launcher answers for health; all of them reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP through the request transport. The server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

variants.name: TASK-526.04
variants.summary: render --track makes a tracked embed that its board lists

nodes.name: Bootstrap
nodes.responsibility: Takes the server address out of argv into the environment before any module that reads it loads, and moves a leading -C behind the command name

nodes.name: Command catalogue
nodes.responsibility: The one table of commands: what exists, what it takes and who owns it

nodes.name: Command routing
nodes.responsibility: Addresses one command, captures the global flags and bounds the run

nodes.name: Contract execution
nodes.responsibility: Parses and validates a command's input, runs its handler with the prerequisites it asks for, and presents the answer
nodes.description: runner.ts is the seam callers import; the steps live here. A command that takes -C answers with the vault it used and how it was found, beside a JSON object answer.

nodes.name: Semantic authoring
nodes.responsibility: The board list, new, edit, branch and show: the commands that state a board and read it back

nodes.name: Board client
nodes.responsibility: The board routes: reads, writes, renders and the vault check, and the refusals they come back with

nodes.name: Runtime control
nodes.responsibility: start, stop and restart: the server as a detached child of this command

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Owns every board and answers every command that reads or writes one

nodes.name: Semantic lifecycle
nodes.responsibility: resolve, adopt and shelve: settling a proposal, moving the current designation, setting a proposal aside

nodes.name: Comparison
nodes.responsibility: compare: what one variant changed about the one it came from

nodes.name: Rasterize
nodes.responsibility: rasterize: one board as a PNG, headlessly, at native scale
nodes.description: Asks the Archboard server for the SVG, as render does, then takes that SVG into a headless browser here and photographs it. With --clipboard, rasterize publishes PNG and self-contained HTML to the local desktop through a native clipboard helper. With --against it draws relative to the variant named, as render does. Its receipt names what the picture draws and marks, as render's does.

nodes.name: Vault check
nodes.responsibility: check with its subcommands all, semantics and code, and semantic config: each check fills its own part of one answer, and the vault's vocabulary and everything wrong with its boards

nodes.name: Claims
nodes.responsibility: claim and release: holding a board for a stretch of agent work

nodes.name: Panes
nodes.responsibility: browser: the live session, its panes with the repository and checkout of each, and pointing one at a board, which makes the caller's checkout the chosen one
nodes.description: browser show from a known checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository makes it the chosen one for the whole machine, and its answer's chose names the checkout it replaced. browser panes reports each pane's vault, repository and checkout, and own: whether the pane shows the vault a command run here finds. The checkout of a pane or of a shown board is always the directory that holds its vault: the checkout root, or the holder of an untracked vault. It finds that vault without refusing or registering, so it still needs no vault.

nodes.name: Board rasterizer
nodes.responsibility: One headless browser, one PNG at a time, refused rather than cropped

nodes.name: Entry point
nodes.responsibility: Hands the command to the archboard checkout it stands in, if that is not the running source; else takes --url out before configuration loads, refuses a removed environment variable and runs the table
nodes.description: TASK-472.09. EXPRESS_SERVER_URL and a set ARCHBOARD_VAULT are refused with exit 2, unless the call asks for help, so a variable that is no longer read never addresses another vault or server than the person means.

nodes.name: Server client
nodes.responsibility: Provides the typed health, claim, pane, and board-refusal operations that commands use
nodes.description: These operations call the shared request transport. The transport handles server identity and errors and reads the invocation context for request addressing.

nodes.name: Render
nodes.responsibility: render: a board, a variant or one of its views as the SVG the Archboard server draws
nodes.description: With --against it reads the board, resolves the variant named as compare does and draws the picture relative to it, without the Planned frame. The receipt names every node, edge, flow and step the picture draws, how each stands, and the counts of the marks its key shows.

nodes.name: Inspect
nodes.responsibility: inspect: one configured group of a board, its members and what crosses its boundary

nodes.name: Rename
nodes.responsibility: rename: another name for a board or one of its variants, the old name kept opening it

nodes.name: Record
nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts). The page it records names the found vault's repository as repoA, and a checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository is refused.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each
nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. The receipt's setup names the repository, its vault, whether the vault was made, whether git ignores it and the documents an earlier block was removed from. --vault, --doc and --yes are gone, and --no-setup, once --no-doc, leaves the repository alone.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.responsibility: status: whether the Archboard server answers, who it is, and what it reports

nodes.name: Replay
nodes.responsibility: replay: a kept talk rendered to a video file again, in either theme, with no voice
nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. A talk that cannot be read is refused as a usage error before a browser starts. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones record uses (lib/recording-output.ts).

nodes.name: Command contract
nodes.responsibility: Runs one bound command contract: parse, prerequisites, handler, presentation; callers reach it only through its root files
nodes.description: Callers outside import only the root files of src/cli/command-contract. runner.ts exports runCommand, the one call the router makes; it passes straight on to executeCommand in lib/execution.ts, which is private. bootstrap.ts and status.ts are root files too: the bootstrap bin.ts runs first, and the status command contract.

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.name: Locality
nodes.responsibility: Ranks parts by commits that changed their bound declarations or paths, labels path-wide fallback, and lists pairs that change together

nodes.name: Footprint
nodes.responsibility: Prints the parts a commit range changed against a proposal, with declaration attribution or explicit path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Server launcher
nodes.responsibility: Starts the Archboard server, which needs no vault, as a detached child when nothing answers, and stops it

nodes.name: Prerequisites
nodes.responsibility: Makes sure what a command needs is there: the server, started when it is not running, and an open canvas

nodes.name: Image clipboard
nodes.responsibility: Publishes PNG and HTML to the native desktop clipboard; retains Linux ownership until another copy replaces it
nodes.description: Uses @teddyzhu/clipboard on Linux and macOS. A detached Bun process owns Linux clipboard data after the command exits. macOS retains the data itself.

nodes.name: Clipboard image
nodes.responsibility: Builds escaped image HTML and its accessible description from the captured board

nodes.name: Source checkout
nodes.responsibility: Which archboard checkout this process runs and the port of its server: 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree; hands a command to the bin/archboard of the checkout it stands in
nodes.description: The main checkout has a .git directory; a linked worktree has a .git file and takes 10000 + sha256(root path) mod 10000. The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. The hand-off follows the working directory, not -C, and does not happen when the environment sets ARCHBOARD_URL: the URL already names the server, and every Codex thread sets it, so a workhorse in another archboard checkout runs the server's own source (ADR 0050). It waits for the other checkout's command, passes SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP on to it and answers with its exit status, and it refuses a checkout with no node_modules, naming the bun install to run there.

nodes.name: Move
nodes.responsibility: semantic move: the whole board into the vault found from --to, as -C finds one, and every drill-down the move rewrote
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051. --expect-version is required, as for every write. A --to holder the registry does not know is registered, and the answer says so. A move that stopped part way names the drill-downs it rewrote already; the same move run again finishes it.

nodes.name: Removed variables
nodes.responsibility: Names the environment variables archboard no longer reads and the refusal for each, which says what to do instead

nodes.name: Repository setup
nodes.responsibility: Makes the .archboard/vault of the git checkout that holds the directory when it has none, and takes the block an earlier version wrote out of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, changing nothing else in the file
nodes.description: Only a begin marker and an end marker that each stand on a line of their own bound a block, across CRLF line endings and never past another begin marker. A marker quoted inside a line is prose and stays, and so does a begin marker whose end marker is gone.

nodes.name: Command startup
nodes.responsibility: Takes argv from the process to one selected command: hands over to the checkout whose source runs, refuses a removed environment variable, finds the command in the table and bounds its run

nodes.name: Server access
nodes.responsibility: Every reach to the Archboard server: the one request path, the board routes with their refusals, starting the server when nothing answers, and restarting it on a new bundle

nodes.name: Pictures and video
nodes.responsibility: What a command produces as a picture or a video outside the server: a headless browser makes the PNG, the recorder makes the narrated video, and the clipboard takes the image

nodes.name: Views
nodes.responsibility: views: every view of a board, with what each draws at a variant
nodes.description: Draws the overview, every authored view and Everything through the render route that render uses, and reports for each what the picture places (nodes, edges, flows and steps), the marks its key counts and its size. A view that draws nothing on the variant is listed with nothing drawn. --variant, --against and --no-comparison read as render reads them.

nodes.name: Restart
nodes.responsibility: Stops the server, builds the frontend from this checkout, and starts the server again
nodes.description: It refuses a server that it could not start again before it stops it, and a refused stop leaves the bundle unbuilt. A failed build refuses with FRONTEND_BUILD_FAILED, carries the build's output and says that the server is stopped. The answer names the entry script of the new bundle, as /health reports it.

nodes.name: Request transport
nodes.responsibility: Sends JSON requests, rejects a server from another checkout, and reports transport errors

nodes.name: Invocation context
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the board, vault, doing line, expected version, and writing session for one CLI invocation

nodes.name: Historical correction
nodes.responsibility: Suggests historical commits, previews corrections and writes checked corrections

nodes.name: Embeds check
nodes.responsibility: Finds the board renders that Git tracks in this checkout and the tracked embeds of the vault's boards, draws each again from its recipe and reports or redraws the outdated ones

nodes.name: Tracked embed
nodes.responsibility: --track on render and rasterize: names the file by its checkout's repository and path, refuses one no repository keeps, and lists it on the board before it is written

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts). The page it records names the found vault's repository as repoA, and a checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository is refused.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each
nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts). The page it records names the found vault's repository as repoA, and a checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository is refused.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each
nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. The receipt's setup names the repository, its vault, whether the vault was made, whether git ignores it and the documents an earlier block was removed from. --vault, --doc and --yes are gone, and --no-setup, once --no-doc, leaves the repository alone.

nodes.name: Replay

nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.name: Panes

nodes.name: Entry point
nodes.responsibility: Hands the command to the archboard checkout it stands in, if that is not the running source; else takes --url out before configuration loads, refuses a removed environment variable and runs the table
nodes.description: TASK-472.09. EXPRESS_SERVER_URL and a set ARCHBOARD_VAULT are refused with exit 2, unless the call asks for help, so a variable that is no longer read never addresses another vault or server than the person means.

nodes.name: Server client
nodes.responsibility: Provides the typed health, claim, pane, and board-refusal operations that commands use
nodes.description: These operations call the shared request transport. The transport handles server identity and errors and reads the invocation context for request addressing.

nodes.name: Render
nodes.responsibility: render: a board, a variant or one of its views as the SVG the Archboard server draws
nodes.description: With --against it reads the board, resolves the variant named as compare does and draws the picture relative to it, without the Planned frame. The receipt names every node, edge, flow and step the picture draws, how each stands, and the counts of the marks its key shows.

nodes.name: Inspect
nodes.responsibility: inspect: one configured group of a board, its members and what crosses its boundary

nodes.name: Rename
nodes.responsibility: rename: another name for a board or one of its variants, the old name kept opening it

nodes.name: Record
nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts). The page it records names the found vault's repository as repoA, and a checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository is refused.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg
nodes.description: It proves an ffmpeg first: the one ARCHBOARD_FFMPEG names, else one on PATH, else nixpkgs#ffmpeg-headless run through Nix, and refuses before any browser starts without one. The talk is kept before its picture is drawn, so a render that fails can be rendered again with replay.

nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each
nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. The receipt's setup names the repository, its vault, whether the vault was made, whether git ignores it and the documents an earlier block was removed from. --vault, --doc and --yes are gone, and --no-setup, once --no-doc, leaves the repository alone.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.responsibility: status: whether the Archboard server answers, who it is, and what it reports

nodes.name: Replay
nodes.responsibility: replay: a kept talk rendered to a video file again, in either theme, with no voice
nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. A talk that cannot be read is refused as a usage error before a browser starts. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones record uses (lib/recording-output.ts).

nodes.name: Command contract
nodes.responsibility: Runs one bound command contract: parse, prerequisites, handler, presentation; callers reach it only through its root files
nodes.description: Callers outside import only the root files of src/cli/command-contract. runner.ts exports runCommand, the one call the router makes; it passes straight on to executeCommand in lib/execution.ts, which is private. bootstrap.ts and status.ts are root files too: the bootstrap bin.ts runs first, and the status command contract.

nodes.name: Commands
nodes.responsibility: The command table and every command family's contracts and handlers
nodes.description: Each file at the root of src/cli/commands is one command family's entry: run.ts holds the table that bin.ts runs, and the others export the contracts whose handlers Contract execution calls. Their private helpers under lib/ are not drawn.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.name: Locality

nodes.name: Footprint
nodes.responsibility: Prints the parts a commit range changed against a proposal, with declaration attribution or explicit path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Server launcher
nodes.responsibility: Starts the Archboard server, which needs no vault, as a detached child when nothing answers, and stops it

nodes.name: Prerequisites
nodes.responsibility: Makes sure what a command needs is there: the server, started when it is not running, and an open canvas

nodes.name: Image clipboard
nodes.responsibility: Publishes PNG and HTML to the native desktop clipboard; retains Linux ownership until another copy replaces it
nodes.description: Uses @teddyzhu/clipboard on Linux and macOS. A detached Bun process owns Linux clipboard data after the command exits. macOS retains the data itself.

nodes.name: Clipboard image
nodes.responsibility: Builds escaped image HTML and its accessible description from the captured board

nodes.name: Source checkout
nodes.responsibility: Which archboard checkout this process runs and the port of its server: 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree; hands a command to the bin/archboard of the checkout it stands in
nodes.description: The main checkout has a .git directory; a linked worktree has a .git file and takes 10000 + sha256(root path) mod 10000. The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. The hand-off follows the working directory, not -C, and does not happen when the environment sets ARCHBOARD_URL: the URL already names the server, and every Codex thread sets it, so a workhorse in another archboard checkout runs the server's own source (ADR 0050). nodes.name: Move
nodes.responsibility: semantic move: the whole board into the vault found from --to, as -C finds one, and every drill-down the move rewrote
nodes.description: TASK-472.15, ADR 0051. --expect-version is required, as for every write. A --to holder the registry does not know is registered, and the answer says so. A move that stopped part way names the drill-downs it rewrote already; the same move run again finishes it.

nodes.name: Removed variables
nodes.responsibility: Names the environment variables archboard no longer reads and the refusal for each, which says what to do instead

nodes.name: Repository setup
nodes.responsibility: Makes the .archboard/vault of the git checkout that holds the directory when it has none, and takes the block an earlier version wrote out of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, changing nothing else in the file
nodes.description: Only a begin marker and an end marker that each stand on a line of their own bound a block, across CRLF line endings and never past another begin marker. A marker quoted inside a line is prose and stays, and so does a begin marker whose end marker is gone.

nodes.name: Command startup
nodes.responsibility: Takes argv from the process to one selected command: hands over to the checkout whose source runs, refuses a removed environment variable, finds the command in the table and bounds its run

nodes.name: Server access

nodes.name: Pictures and video
nodes.responsibility: What a command produces as a picture or a video outside the server: a headless browser makes the PNG, the recorder makes the narrated video, and the clipboard takes the image

nodes.name: Views
nodes.responsibility: views: every view of a board, with what each draws at a variant
nodes.description: Draws the overview, every authored view and Everything through the render route that render uses, and reports for each what the picture places (nodes, edges, flows and steps), the marks its key counts and its size. A view that draws nothing on the variant is listed with nothing drawn. --variant, --against and --no-comparison read as render reads them.

nodes.name: Restart

nodes.description: It refuses a server that it could not start again before it stops it, and a refused stop leaves the bundle unbuilt. A failed build refuses with FRONTEND_BUILD_FAILED, carries the build's output and says that the server is stopped. The answer names the entry script of the new bundle, as /health reports it.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, health, claims and panes through the server client, and both reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP; the server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

beats.heading: One catalogue defines the surface
beats.body: Every command this CLI has is a row of one table, with the contract that says what it takes. Nothing is registered anywhere else, so help, routing and execution cannot disagree about what exists. Inside another archboard checkout, the entry point first hands the command to that checkout's own bin/archboard, so a worktree runs its own source against its own server. Then it takes --url out, because the modules that talk to the server read its address as they load.

beats.heading: The contract bounds the invocation
beats.body: Input is validated against the contract before a handler runs, a prerequisite the handler asks for is ensured once, so a server that is not running is started, and the answer is presented one way for every command.

beats.heading: Persistence stays in the server
beats.body: No command writes a vault file. Board operations go through the board client, claims and panes through theirs, and the server launcher answers for health; all of them reach the Archboard server as JSON over HTTP through the request transport. The server owns the file, the lease and the version check. What the CLI keeps itself is this machine's list of repository checkouts.

beats.heading: Three commands draw for themselves
beats.body: Rasterize asks the Archboard server for the SVG like every other command, then photographs it in a headless browser of its own. Record hands a walkthrough to the recorder: the server's own page plays it while the Codex voice narrates, and the recorder keeps that talk. A second browser then draws the talk frame by frame, and ffmpeg makes the video file. Replay renders a kept talk again, with no voice.

nodes.name: Claims
nodes.responsibility: claim and release: holding a board for a stretch of agent work

nodes.name: Panes
nodes.responsibility: browser: the live session, its panes with the repository and checkout of each, and pointing one at a board, which makes the caller's checkout the chosen one

nodes.name: Board rasterizer
nodes.responsibility: One headless browser, one PNG at a time, refused rather than cropped

nodes.name: Entry point
nodes.responsibility: Hands the command to the archboard checkout it stands in, if that is not the running source; else takes --url out before configuration loads, refuses a removed environment variable and runs the table
nodes.description: TASK-472.09. EXPRESS_SERVER_URL and a set ARCHBOARD_VAULT are refused with exit 2, unless the call asks for help, so a variable that is no longer read never addresses another vault or server than the person means.

nodes.name: Server client
nodes.responsibility: Reads what the server reports about itself, its health and its sync status, and shows a refused board request the way the CLI prints it
nodes.description: Health and sync status ask the shared request transport, which handles server identity and errors. The claim, pane and board routes have clients of their own.

nodes.name: Render
nodes.responsibility: render: a board, a variant or one of its views as the SVG the Archboard server draws
nodes.description: With --against it reads the board, resolves the variant named as compare does and draws the picture relative to it, without the Planned frame. The receipt names every node, edge, flow and step the picture draws, how each stands, and the counts of the marks its key shows.

nodes.name: Inspect
nodes.responsibility: inspect: one configured group of a board, its members and what crosses its boundary

nodes.name: Rename
nodes.responsibility: rename: another name for a board or one of its variants, the old name kept opening it

nodes.name: Record
nodes.responsibility: record: one walkthrough, narrated by the Codex voice, to a video file
nodes.description: Reads the board and the vault policy through the Archboard server and hands the walkthrough to the recorder, which keeps the talk it records in the state directory, or where --talk says. With --discard it deletes a board made only to be recorded once the file is written, and keeps one somebody changed meanwhile. With --against every frame marks only what the variant changes over the one named, resolved as compare resolves it, and the talk keeps that variant. Its --out checks and its refusals of the browser and ffmpeg are the ones replay uses (lib/recording-output.ts). The page it records names the found vault's repository as repoA, and a checkout that is not the chosen one of its repository is refused.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recorder
nodes.responsibility: Records a walkthrough's talk on the Archboard server's own page, then draws it frame by frame in a second private headless browser and encodes the file through ffmpeg

nodes.name: Repositories
nodes.responsibility: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the servers configured for each
nodes.description: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server lives in repo-language-server.ts.

nodes.name: Install skill
nodes.responsibility: install-skill: copies the bundled skills into a skills root and makes this repository's vault, writing nothing into its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
nodes.description: TASK-471.03. A command finds the vault from the repository it runs in (ADR 0049), so nothing about it is written down. --repo, else the working directory, names a directory, and the vault is made at the root of the git checkout that holds it, where a command run anywhere in the checkout finds it. The receipt's setup names the repository, its vault, whether the vault was made, whether git ignores it and the documents an earlier block was removed from. --vault, --doc and --yes are gone, and --no-setup, once --no-doc, leaves the repository alone.

nodes.name: Status

nodes.name: Replay

nodes.description: Needs the Archboard server only for the page it draws in. The board need not exist, and no Codex is involved. nodes.name: Commands

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.responsibility: The seam a selected contract is run through, with the argv and the abort signal
nodes.description: The module's public entry point. It passes the call straight on to executeCommand; the execution steps behind it are private (runner.ts).

nodes.name: Locality

nodes.name: Footprint
nodes.responsibility: Prints the parts a commit range changed against a proposal, with declaration attribution or explicit path-wide fallback

nodes.name: Server launcher
nodes.responsibility: Starts the Archboard server, which needs no vault, as a detached child when nothing answers, stops it, and says what answers at its address and how many browsers look at it

nodes.name: Prerequisites
nodes.responsibility: Makes sure what a command needs is there: the server, started when it is not running, and an open canvas

nodes.name: Image clipboard
nodes.responsibility: Publishes PNG and HTML to the native desktop clipboard; retains Linux ownership until another copy replaces it
nodes.description: Uses @teddyzhu/clipboard on Linux and macOS. A detached Bun process owns Linux clipboard data after the command exits. macOS retains the data itself.

nodes.name: Clipboard image
nodes.responsibility: Builds escaped image HTML and its accessible description from the captured board

nodes.name: Source checkout
nodes.responsibility: Which archboard checkout this process runs and the port of its server: 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree; hands a command to the bin/archboard of the checkout it stands in

The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. The hand-off follows the working directory, not -C, and does not happen when the environment sets ARCHBOARD_URL: the URL already names the server, and every Codex thread sets it, so a workhorse in another archboard checkout runs the server's own source (ADR 0050). nodes.name: Removed variables
nodes.responsibility: Names the environment variables archboard no longer reads and the refusal for each, which says what to do instead

nodes.name: Repository setup
nodes.responsibility: Makes the .archboard/vault of the git checkout that holds the directory when it has none, and takes the block an earlier version wrote out of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, changing nothing else in the file
nodes.description: Only a begin marker and an end marker that each stand on a line of their own bound a block, across CRLF line endings and never past another begin marker. A marker quoted inside a line is prose and stays, and so does a begin marker whose end marker is gone.

nodes.responsibility: Takes argv from the process to one selected command: hands over to the checkout whose source runs, refuses a removed environment variable, finds the command in the table and bounds its run

nodes.name: Pictures and video
nodes.responsibility: What a command produces as a picture or a video outside the server: a headless browser makes the PNG, the recorder makes the narrated video, and the clipboard takes the image

nodes.name: Views
nodes.responsibility: views: every view of a board, with what each draws at a variant
nodes.description: Draws the overview, every authored view and Everything through the render route that render uses, and reports for each what the picture places (nodes, edges, flows and steps), the marks its key counts and its size. A view that draws nothing on the variant is listed with nothing drawn. --variant, --against and --no-comparison read as render reads them.

nodes.name: Restart
nodes.responsibility: Stops the server, builds the frontend from this checkout, and starts the server again
nodes.description: It refuses a server that it could not start again before it stops it, and a refused stop leaves the bundle unbuilt. A failed build refuses with FRONTEND_BUILD_FAILED, carries the build's output and says that the server is stopped. The answer names the entry script of the new bundle, as /health reports it.

nodes.responsibility: Sends JSON requests, rejects a server from another checkout, and reports transport errors

nodes.name: Invocation context
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the board, vault, doing line, expected version, and writing session for one CLI invocation

nodes.name: Historical correction
nodes.responsibility: Suggests historical commits, previews corrections and writes checked corrections

nodes.responsibility: The claim routes: taking a board for a stretch of agent work, and giving it back

nodes.name: Pane client
nodes.responsibility: The pane routes: the panes on screen, one more pane, closing one, and pointing one at a board as an agent

nodes.name: Stated change
nodes.responsibility: Reads the change a write states, once for edit and resolve: the version first, then the input as a JSON object, then the variant it names, saying an override at once

nodes.name: Embeds check
nodes.responsibility: Draws each render that Git tracks here and each tracked embed of the vault's boards again from its recipe, and reports or redraws the outdated ones; fetches a vault no checkout here holds

nodes.name: Tracked embed
nodes.responsibility: --track on render and rasterize: names the file by its checkout's repository and path, refuses one no repository keeps, and lists it on the board before it is written

nodes.name: Vault repository
nodes.responsibility: The Git remote of a repository that this machine has no checkout of, whose default branch holds the vault an embed names

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.responsibility: Deletes a board through the board client, refused while another board opens it

nodes.name: Model read

nodes.name: Model checkpoint commands
nodes.responsibility: Retains observed revisions and lists local checkpoint metadata

nodes.name: Canonical model client
nodes.responsibility: Preserves shared read, retain and list outcomes across HTTP, including structured refusals

nodes.name: Migration planning

nodes.name: Migration planning client
nodes.responsibility: Carries explicit vault requests and shared inventory or refusal contracts over HTTP

nodes.name: Model publication commands
nodes.responsibility: Configures, publishes, fetches and reports archive history through the shared runtime
